fitted.already_on_this_board: D10, D11 and D12 carry this exact MPN and LCSC code, procurement-locked at D-211. D14 therefore joins an existing BOM line: no new part, no new feeder, no new footprint.

facts.table: Electrical Characteristics (@TA = +25 C, unless otherwise specified)
facts.why_the_0p1mA_row_is_the_one_used: the held gate draws about 9 uA through R132, which is BELOW the lowest published forward-current row; VF is monotonically increasing in IF, so VF(9 uA) <= VF(0.1 mA) = 240 mV is a GUARANTEED bound and needs no interpolation
facts.why_the_25V_reverse_row_is_a_bound_here: IR increases with VR, and this node never exceeds the held gate of about 2.17 V, so the 25 V row is an upper bound at 25 C. The 40 C top of the prototype envelope is carried by a DECLARED 3x factor, which is above the conventional doubling-per-10-K rule for a Schottky.

fitted.obtained_via: the dataManualUrl of the live D-096 JLCPCB record evidence/jlc-live/bat54ws-7-f-00947faf.json (C124205, Diodes Incorporated, stock 82659)

polarity_correction.checked_by: checks/demo_feature_contract.py F5, which computes the true-off floor and the leak-aware ordering and refuses the 1N4148WS at this rail by arithmetic
polarity_correction.what_d752_said: 1N4148WS chosen over a Schottky BECAUSE OF ITS REVERSE LEAKAGE: ... A BAT54WS would have put that floor near or above threshold at temperature on an UNPUBLISHED number.
polarity_correction.what_the_schottky_actually_costs: ordering margin, not true-off. The larger reverse leakage discharges C85 in parallel with R132, so demo_feature_contract F5 solves the hold decay with a CONSTANT-CURRENT leak beside the exponential rather than with R132 alone.
polarity_correction.why_it_is_superseded: the sign is wrong. KiCad's Device:D has pin 1 = K and pin 2 = A, and the board wires D14 pin 1 to /03_SPI_A_DISPLAY_SD/BL_DISC_G (Q11's gate) and pin 2 to /DISP_BL_CTL. In the true-off state CTRL is driven LOW and the gate sits above it, so D14 is REVERSE biased and its leakage flows K->A, OUT of the gate. It can only pull the gate DOWN. The only current that can hold the gate up is Q11's own IGSS, <= 100 nA, which across R132's 222.2 kOhm worst case is 22.2 mV against the SQ2364EES's VGS(th) MINIMUM of 0.46 V.

facts.why_it_is_superseded: 715 mV is the LOWEST published forward-voltage maximum and the part publishes no row below 1 mA. Held gate = VOH(0.8 x 3.069408 V) - VF - a declared 2 mV/K allowance to the 0 C prototype endpoint = 1.690526 V, so VGS = 1.486526 V against the fitted SQ2364EES's only published low-gate RDS(on) condition of VGS = 1.5 V. It is short by 13.5 mV and there is no lower-current row to bound it with.

temperature_allowance.why: both documents publish their forward-voltage tables at Ta = 25 C only. A silicon PN junction's VF rises about 2 mV/K as temperature falls and a Schottky's rises less; 2.0 mV/K is applied to BOTH so the comparison between them is like-for-like and the allowance is conservative for the Schottky. 0 C is the bottom of the declared 0..40 C prototype qualification envelope.

unit_check: the extracted .txt of both documents was checked against the PDF for the micro->m / Ohm->W substitution D-779 found in another vendor .txt; the quoted rows carry only mV, uA, nA and pF and are unaffected
vendor_correction: D-790 / D789-A08.  This field read 'Jiangsu Changjing Electronics Technology Co., Ltd. (JSCJ)', which is the manufacturer of the SUPERSEDED 1N4148WS and never of the fitted part.  The record's own `fitted` block always said Diodes Incorporated BAT54WS-7-F; the top-level vendor field had not followed it.  The superseded part's manufacturer is recorded in `superseded.manufacturer`.
why: D788-11 asked for Q11's held gate to be DERIVED from the rail, the GPIO VOH, D14's forward drop, C85/R132 and leakage rather than asserted at a constant 2.60 V left over from the 3.3 V rail. Deriving it showed the 1N4148WS no longer fits: at the D-788 rail the held VGS bounds to 1.4865 V against the SQ2364EES's only published low-gate conduction row of VGS = 1.5 V. D14 therefore changes from a silicon switching diode to a Schottky in the SAME SOD-323 land, from the SAME manufacturer already fitted on this reference. Both documents are archived: the part that leaves and the part that arrives.
